annotationRationale: Substituting 1 and reciprocal inputs into the functional equation establishes the quotient rule. Prime factorizations then determine all five values.
sourceMethod: Follows the official derivation of f(1), reciprocal values, and sums of prime factors, followed by evaluation of every choice.

review.mathCheck: Substitution gives f(1)=0 and f(1/r)=−f(r), hence f(a/b)=f(a)−f(b). Prime-factor multiplicities give the five values 7, 3, 1, 2, and −1. Only 25/11 qualifies, choice E.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 18 on page 11: establish the identity and reciprocal values, then evaluate every choice through prime factors. No unstated regularity assumption is introduced.
review.annotationCheck: Functional-equation substitutions are correctly assessed, with prime factorization as supporting knowledge. Repeated factors and every answer choice are explained sufficiently.
